gloss: to open one's mouth; to open (a container)

definitions.gloss: to open one's mouth (to speak, yawn, or receive food, medicine, or a dental exam)
definitions.explanation: The basic, literal sense: to physically open the mouth. Commonly heard at the dentist ({口|くち}を{大|おお}きく{開|あ}けてください), when feeding a baby or an animal, or when describing someone yawning or singing. Note: for the sense 'to start talking; to speak up', Japanese usually prefers {口|くち}を{開|ひら}く with the reading ひらく.

definitions.gloss: to open (a bottle, package, or other container); to unseal
definitions.explanation: By extension from the 'mouth' metaphor for openings: to remove the cap or seal of a bottle, jar, bag, or similar container, often for the first time. Common with foods, drinks, cosmetics, and medicines.

examples.japanese: {口|くち}を{開|あ}けてください。
{赤|あか}ちゃんが{口|くち}を{開|あ}けてあくびをした。
examples.english: The baby opened its mouth and yawned.

examples.japanese: {歯医者|はいしゃ}さんに「もう{少|すこ}し{大|おお}きく{口|くち}を{開|あ}けて」と{言|い}われて、{必死|ひっし}であごを{広|ひろ}げた。
examples.english: When the dentist said 'Please open your mouth a little wider,' I spread my jaws open for all I was worth.

examples.japanese: ワインの{口|くち}を{開|あ}ける。
examples.english: To open a bottle of wine.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{醤油|しょうゆ}の{口|くち}を{開|あ}けたら、{香|かお}りが{立|た}った。
examples.english: When I opened the new bottle of soy sauce, the aroma wafted up.

examples.japanese: お{土産|みやげ}にもらったジャムの{瓶|びん}の{口|くち}を{開|あ}けたら、{甘|あま}い{香|かお}りが{部屋|へや}いっぱいに{広|ひろ}がった。
examples.english: When I opened the jar of jam that I had received as a souvenir, a sweet aroma filled the entire room.

notes:
The construction is noun {口|くち} + を + verb {開|あ}ける. {口|くち} here refers literally to the mouth (sense 1) or to the opening/mouth of a container (sense 2); {開|あ}ける is the transitive verb 'to open'.

USAGE:
- Sense 1 is nearly always concrete and physical. The metaphorical 'open one's mouth = start speaking' sense is normally carried by {口|くち}を{開|ひら}く (same kanji, but read ひらく). Beginning learners often conflate them.
- For the intransitive counterpart (a mouth/container opens by itself or is open), use {口|くち}が{開|あ}く or the state form {口|くち}が{開|あ}いている.
- In sense 2, {口|くち}を{切|き}る is a near-synonym, especially for unsealing a new package or bottle for the very first time.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {口|くち}を{大|おお}きく{開|あ}ける: to open one's mouth wide
- {口|くち}を{開|あ}けて{笑|わら}う: to open one's mouth and laugh
- あくびをして{口|くち}を{開|あ}ける: to open one's mouth in a yawn
- ワインの{口|くち}を{開|あ}ける: to open a bottle of wine
- {瓶|びん}の{口|くち}を{開|あ}ける: to open the mouth of a bottle
- {袋|ふくろ}の{口|くち}を{開|あ}ける: to open the mouth of a bag

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {口|くち}を{開|ひら}く: to open one's mouth (and speak); to break one's silence — figurative use, focused on speech.
- {口|くち}を{切|き}る: to be the first to speak; also to unseal a new container — overlaps with sense 2 when referring to opening something for the first time.
- {口|くち}を{閉|と}じる / {閉|し}める: to close one's mouth — the antonym.
- {開|あ}ける: to open — the general transitive verb; combines freely with many objects (door, window, box).
